 Live Updates WWE WWE SmackDown Live Updates, Results and Highlights Before Crown Jewel 2026
 Erik Beaston Nov 6, 2026, updated just now 
 Welcome to B/R's live coverage of the November 6 episode of WWE SmackDown, on the eve of the Crown Jewel premium live event.
 Results included:
 Shinsuke Nakamura defeated Tama Tonga 
 Women's Tag Team Champions B-Fab and Michin fought Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid to a no-contest 
 Damian Priest defeated Nathan Frazer via referee stoppage 
 Tap in, scroll through, and follow along with all of the action from the Barclays Center in Brooklyn. 
 Live Updates
 17 Total Posts
 Newest First ​ Just Now 10:10 PM Takeaways from Friday's Show
 Punk and Owens Deliver 
 This was realistically a one-match show, with Punk vs. Owens hyped for weeks. Thankfully, it more than delivered. It was a fantastic, physically violent match that saw each man punish the other, throwing their finishers at them until one man could not take any more.
 That man was Punk, who continues to tell the story of a former champion desperate to get back there but constantly sidetracked by Owens and other ghosts of his past.
 Owens is suddenly in world title contention, and the fact that his best friend currently holds the title suggests the rekindling of that rivalry may not be far off. 
 Women's War Games Tease 
 Based on how often The Judgment Day's Roxanne Perez, Raquel Rodriguez, and Liv Morgan have been intertwined with Iyo Sky, Chelsea Green, and Tiffany Stratton, it felt like that was the direction things were heading with the Survivor Series: War Games on the horizon.
 Instead, it looks like some mixture of Jade Cargill, Michin, B-Fab, and Fatal Influence will team to battle Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, and Bayley in the namesake match.
 It is not a bad idea for a roster that has been intertwined so intricately, for better or worse, but it feels rather inconsequential.
 What Crown Jewel Hype? 
 Outside of some rather generic video packages, there was very little substance in terms of genuine Premium Live Event hype. Nothing was advanced, there were no new developments. For the most part, the matches on the card were highlighted quickly or not at all, with Punk vs. Owens taking center stage.
 On that front, it failed.
 9 mins ago 10:01 PM Punk vs. Owens, continued
 Punk wrapped his knee in a steel chain, looking to increase the damage, but Owens cut him off and drove his opponent down. He set up six chairs, stuck Punk on the top rope, and teased delivering a superplex.
 Instead, Punk drove him off the top and back-first into the chairs. He failed, though, to keep KO down.
 Punk teased an apron Go To Sleep, but Owens countered out and delivered a Fisherman's Buster from the ring apron through the table at ringside.
 Back inside, he delivered the Stunner, but Punk kicked out at two against all odds. 
 Frustrated, KO wrapped the steel chain around his hand and yelled, "Die, you piece of s**t!" Punk grabbed hold of him, delivered the Go To Sleep, but Owens rebounded and rocked his rival with a chain-assisted right hand.
 He covered for three and the victory.
 WINNER: KEVIN OWENS 
 This was a good, physical, high-impact, highly physical bout and a suitable main event that played to the intensity and dislike between the two Superstars.
 Owens stood tall to close the show out.
 19 mins ago 09:52 PM No Holds Barred: CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens
 Some final hype for Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing Match aired via video package.
 CM Punk and Kevin Owens hit the ring for their No Holds Barred Match main event, a contest that easily could have headlined its own PLE.
 The fight spilled outside early, slamming Owens off the announce table, only for the Prizefighter to recover quickly and catch him with a chair to the midsection. From there, the brawl relocated to the stands, where Punk laid into Owens with some hard rights and lefts, only to be ground into a piece of plexiglass and thrown over a trash can.
 "He was standing on a rather tender area," Wade Barrett said to describe The Prizefighter's attack on the Best in the World.
 Back at ringside, Punk delivered a shot to the face with the ring steps, then fell victim to the same weapon as Owens blocked a piledriver and tripped his opponent up back-first onto the steel.
 Owens rocked Punk with a steel chair in between setting up tables at ringside. From there, he weathered a momentary onslaught to place a trash can over Punk's head and deliver a cannonball in the corner amid chants of "one more time."
 Moments later, the fight spilled up the aisle and to the video screen, where Owens sent Punk into his own picture. He tried for a piledriver, but Punk delivered the GTS. Unable to pin him on the floor, Punk put him on a rolling cart and sent Owens back to the squared circle on it.
 Punk added a Macho Man-style elbow drop and applied the Anaconda Vise, but Owens raked the face and forced the break.
 A spike DDT on a steel chair followed, but Owens kicked out at two. The former WWE champion buried his opponent under plunder but Owens rolled outside of the ring, to the sanctuary of the floor. 
 With Owens sprawled on the announce table, Punk walked the guardrail and proceeded to drive an elbow on Owens, through the announce table.
 45 mins ago 09:25 PM Nathan Frazer vs. Damian Priest
 Born of Fraxiom's assist to an injured R-Truth two weeks ago, and a backstage confrontation last week, Nathan Frazer squared off with Damian Priest in singles action.
 The commentary team put over Priest's ambition to get back to world title contention, laying the groundwork for the change in attitude of late.
 Frazer started fast and furiously, sticking and moving, never allowing Priest to strike or get hold of him.
 Priest ended that in short order, rocking him with a hard right forearm. The Archer of Infamy caught him in mid-flight and sent him into the guardrail. From there, Priest delivered a Razor's Edge across the announce table.
 With the babyface unable to continue, the referee called for the end of the match.
 WINNER: PRIEST VIA REFEREE STOPPAGE 
 After the match, Priest launched Axiom into the ring post. 
 53 mins ago 09:17 PM Trick Williams Sends A Message to Damian Priest
 The busy Saxton caught up with United States Champion Trick Williams, who was flanked by Lil Yachty.
 Williams admitted that he was not where he expected to be as he thought he would be heading to Riyadh to battle Roman Reigns as the Undisputed WWE Champion. 
 From there, Saxton asked about Damian Priest. Yachty cracked a joke and Williams said that if anyone wants a shot at him, they know where to find him. 
 Williams is done taking the disrespect. Hopefully, that means he will show a little more fire and stand up for himself moving forward.
 57 mins ago 09:14 PM Final Hype for Chelsea Green vs. Liv Morgan
 Backstage, Saxton caught up with Bayley, Bliss, Paxley, and Flair. Bayley said she refused to take the disrespect while The Queen laid down the gauntlet, stating that if the two heel factions want to go to war, "so be it." 
 In the arena, SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis introduced WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green and said that, despite their past, he is proud that Green is representing SmackDown and proud of the competitor herself.
 Green admitted that she doubts herself and struggles with believing in herself. She questioned whether she belongs in the same sentence as previous women's champions and admitted that her match tomorrow against Morgan is her chance to prove that she is a worthy and deserving champion.
 "I cement my place as a true champion, Nick," Green said of the implications of a victory.
 Morgan interrupted, mocked Green's emotion, and said, "This is why we don't give participation trophies to people who think they should be champion when they haven't even earned to be champion." 
 She called Green a "talentless person" and said that is why the fans relate to her. 
 "That's not how this works. No, because you are not a champion, Chelsea. You are a charity case. And tomorrow night, I get to prove those voices in your head true when I leave the ring as not only the two-time Crown Jewel Champion, but also the greatest Women's World Champion of allllllllllllllll time!" she said.
 Morgan dropped the mic to end the segment.
 1 hour ago 09:05 PM Kevin Owens Speaks on the Main Event
 Backstage, Byron Saxton caught up with Kevin Owens, who balked at CM Punk asking Shawn Michaels to have him removed from the arena for his NXT Championship Match against Grayson Waller on Wednesday night.
 He said NXT is about the future. The two of them? They're inching closer to being the past. Tonight, he wants to send Punk to the past sooner than the Best in the World wants.
 1 hour ago 09:00 PM Women's Tag Team Championship Match: Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid vs. Michin and B-Fab
 Current and former tag team champions collided in the night's next match as B-Fab and Michin defended their titles against Fatal Influence's Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid.
 Michin and Reid each tried to boot, but they caught each other's feet. They put them down at the same time, then attempted a cheap right hand, which neither could pull off.
 The fun and clever spots ended quickly as B-Fab took the fight to Reid, dropping her with a big clothesline. 
 Henley tagged herself in and immediately found herself on the defensive against a game B-Fab, who showed great fire and determination.
 Before the match could develop, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley hit the ring to draw a disqualification finish.
 RESULT: No contest 
 After the match, Bayley hit the ring seeking a measure of revenge after suffering a beatdown at the hands of B-Fab, Michin, and Jade Cargill Monday night on Raw. The numbers proved to be too great, though, until Charlotte Flair made her return and drove the champions and the challengers to the floor.
 The Queen joined Bliss, Paxley, and Bayley in the squared circle to close things out and tease the women's War Games match. 
 1 hour ago 08:46 PM Gunther Was Totally Not Scared Last Week
 Gunther hit the ring to discuss the events of last week, when Finn Balor dusted off the Demon persona to elicit fear from the Ring General.
 The Ring General said he was not scared but, rather, weirded out by what he saw out of Balor last week.
 He said The Demon embarrassed the sport and said he once had great respect for the Irishman and everything he accomplished. Not so much anymore, now that he is working with Danhausen.
 Balor entered the arena sans the Demon makeup and said that last week, it was fear he saw on Gunther's face.
 As he stepped through the ropes, Balor claimed to have a demon inside waiting to get out. "And I'm done waiting," he said.
 The confrontation turned physical, with Gunther setting Balor up for a powerbomb at one point, only to suffer the Sling Blade. The Prince added a shotgun dropkick and teased Coup de Grace, but the Career Killer rolled to the sanctuary of the floor.
 Balor stood tall to close out the segment.
 1 hour ago 08:39 PM CM Punk Talks Main Event
 Cathy Kelley caught up with CM Punk ahead of his No Holds Barred Match against Kevin Owens.
 The Best in the World noted that he was tired of the "ex-girlfriend energy" of Owens and Sami Zayn, and is ready to regain the Undisputed WWE Championship that has eluded him to this point.
 He is ready to get back to that and if it means wrapping a steel chair around Owens' "fat head," so be it.
 1 hour ago 08:35 PM Nakamura vs. Tonga, continued
 During the break, Tonga dominated the action, grounding Nakamura.
 The artist fought back and rocked Tonga with a kick, then planted his opponent in the center of the ring. He set up for the Kinshasa, but Talla Tonga distracted him.
 Tonga cut off the finisher while Talla set up Kyoki for a big chokeslam on the ring apron. Instead, the babyface sent the giant into the guardrail. Back in the ring, Nakamura delivered the Kinshasa and pinned Tonga for the win.
 WINNER: Nakamura 
 A mostly fine match, this brought us one step closer to Bakusai vs. The MFTs for the tag team titles.
 1 hour ago 08:27 PM Shinsuke Nakamura vs. Tama Tonga
 The rivalry over the WWE Tag Team Championship continued Friday night as Shinsuke Nakamura, representing Bakusai, battled The MFT's Tama Tonga.
 Tonga had early success before Nakamura turned the tide.
 As the fight spilled onto the arena floor, though, The Artist appeared to have momentum on his side.
 A cheap, undetected big boot by Talla Tonga downed Nakamura and gave Tonga the upper hand.
 Commercial break. 
 1 hour ago 08:23 PM Johnny Gargano Props Up The Last Real Good Guy
 Backstage, Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae approached Sami Zayn after the Last Real Good Guy's confrontation with AAA Cruiserweight Champion Rey Fenix.
 Gargano hyped Zayn up before LeRae reminded the WWE champ that he still owes Johnny Wrestling a title shot.
 Zayn feigned caring, saying he would hate to lose his title before Gargano got the shot, which prompted the former NXT titleholder to promise him support. 
 Great, manipulative stuff from Zayn here, though it appears LeRae is beginning to pick up on the insincerity of the heel. 
 1 hour ago 08:18 PM 946 Attacks
 Royce Keys, Jaida Parker, Carmelo Hayes, Cruz Montana, Lucien Prince, and Bronco Nima hit the ring and jumped Uso, beating him down before backing Zayn down and out of the ring.
 Rather than aiding his former friend, the cowardly Zayn walked away, leaving Uso to be further assaulted before the heel faction stood tall to close out the segment. 
 A great look at the cowardly, spineless nature of the heel champion when confronted with anything that could threaten him in any way. 
 1 hour ago 08:14 PM Sami Zayn Addressed the WWE Universe
 Just 24 hours before one of the biggest matches in his career, a champion vs. champion encounter with Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn kicked off Friday's show by taking to the ring to address the WWE Universe.
 "I've gotta know: how many of you here tonight came to ride or die with the Last Real Good Guy?!" Zayn asked to a less-than-enthusiastic response.
 A braggadocious Zayn recalled his attack on Reigns at the end of Raw, reminding fans and The Tribal Chief himself that it was the OTC left looking up at him as Monday's show went off the air.
 Jimmy Uso interrupted, reminding Zayn that he was his dog once upon a time. Monday, though, he was handcuffed and forced to watch as the Undisputed WWE Champion kicked Reigns in the face instead of having his back.
 Zayn reminded Uso that when they were family, it was always Jimmy who "pulled the trigger" and did what he had to do, even if it meant laying him out.
 "You put yourself in the line of fire. You did that," Uso warned Zayn. "He said, 'at Crown Jewel, you're gonna catch this beating. At Crown Jewel, Sami, you're gonna get your ass beat," Uso said on behalf of Reigns.
 "He's going to kick my ass? Good," Zayn said before telling him to tell Reigns he will see him there.
 2 hours ago 08:04 PM Setting the Stage
 Heightened tensions accompanied CM Punk and Kevin Owens' No Holds Barred main event, as did an opening video package hyping it. 
 His eye blackened before the main event, Punk entered the arena, a look of confidence on his face.
 Owens paced back and forth on top of the Barclay's Center while sporting a Finn Balor shirt, his mind clearly racing over his showdown with the Best in the World.
 A recap of Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn's verbal back-and-forth from Monday's Raw aired next.
 2 hours ago 07:47 PM Bakusai's Warning for the MFTs
 Ahead of his match against Tama Tonga, Shinsuke Nakamura and Kyoki had a few words for the WWE Tag Team Champions.
